doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Opening greetings and moving from California to New York in 1961
summary: Rowe welcomes Dodgion; he explains he came to New York in 1961 expecting five years and is still there.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and it’s my great pleasure to have with me saxophonist and reed man Jerry Dodgion. Welcome.
Thank you very much. Nice to be here.
I wonder, you are a Californian originally, right?
I wonder if during these winters here if you ever wish you still were?
Well I’ve been here a little while. I guess I came in 1961, I thought maybe we’d stay about five years. So I think the five years isn’t up yet. This is ‘96. It took 35 years.
You found work here then, to keep you here.
Yeah, well sure. I think New York’s the greatest place in the world if you have a good reason to be here. It’s wonderful.
